The M3.5 implementation is honest and correct: the f32_to_f16 builtin is a single OpFConvert with NO new capability beyond the M3.3c union M2.6 union; the fused kernel does M2.6 dequant -> f32_to_f16 -> shared[f16] -> M3.3c RB coopmat; the frozen 1e-3 was NOT loosened (AT-1770 K=256 PASS 8.3e-4; AT-1771 K=512 3.6e-3 EXCEEDS 1e-3 with gate capped at K=256 and divergence reported separately); the bench reports max_rel_diff at every size including the 29.07 garbage at the A/B shape. 893 tests pass, clippy clean, no regression, llama.cpp not committed. The ~9x throughput gap is now correctly framed as fast-but-WRONG at inference K (correct only at K<=256; needs an f32-accumulator coopmat in M3.5b), NOT a usable-kernel win.
